{{Short description|American statistician}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=April 2021}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=April 2021}}
'''Susan Mary Paddock''' is an American statistician whose publications have included work on [[Nonparametric statistics|nonparametric Bayesian inference]],{{r|mg|2norc}} [[substance abuse]],{{r|2norc}} and the safety of [[autonomous vehicle]]s.{{r|fool}}

Paddock is a graduate of the [[University of Minnesota]] and has a Ph.D. from [[Duke University]].{{r|norc}} Her 1999 doctoral dissertation, ''Randomized Polya Trees: Bayesian Nonparametrics for Multivariate Data Analysis'', was supervised by Mike West.{{r|mg}} Formerly head of the RAND Statistics Group at the [[RAND Corporation]], she moved to [[NORC at the University of Chicago]] in 2019 as chief statistician and executive vice president.{{r|2norc}}

She was named a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2013,{{r|fasa}} and in the same year won the Mid-Career Achievement Award of the  American Statistical Association's Health Policy Statistics Section.{{r|mid}} She was the 2019 chair of the association's Section on Bayesian Statistical Science.{{r|bayes}}
